_comment: Golden fixture for the purchase tribunal. Both the deterministic path and the live three-model path are measured against these exact cases, reason strings included. A fixture defect once looked like a model defect: C06 was written with reason 'test', the models correctly refused for lack of a stated reason, and the run was read as a gate disagreement. Fixing the fixture changed the result, not the code.

cases.item: Vitamin C serum — restock for the skincare line
cases.reason: The current bottle runs out on Thursday; the line ships Friday.
cases.note: Ordinary restock, well inside the month.

cases.reason: Two of five review units are empty and the tester panel starts Monday.
Replacing the current bottle that oxidised after the cap was left open.
cases.note: 60% of the $80 left. Replacing a ruined bottle must not attract a price-cut condition.

cases.reason: A duplicate of a bottle bought eleven days ago.
cases.note: Duplicate. G4 (not a repeat) reads recentPurchases and returns against, so the deterministic path decides CONDITIONAL: the models or the gate both refuse to buy it outright, and no money is released without the condition being met. An earlier expectation of APPROVED here was wrong — a duplicate should never be a plain yes.

cases.reason: The floor is scuffed and the landlord complained.
Current stock covers nine days; the printer needs ten days' notice.
cases.note: 90% of the month in one item. G3 fires on the monthly share, not on the remainder — this is G3 doing its own job, not a headroom condition.

cases.item: Licence renewal — design software, one seat
cases.reason: The seat expires on the 30th and the designer uses it daily.
Three buyers asked for samples before committing to a wholesale order.
cases.note: 22% of the $100 left, tied to a stated buyer request.

cases.item: Temperature logger for the storage room
cases.reason: Last week's heat spike reached 31C and no record exists to prove otherwise.
The current caps leak on one in twenty bottles.
cases.note: 100% of the $12 left. Tiny amount, no headroom: the case that proves the share, not the amount, is what matters.
